newsitem.title: RUSSIA: New Russian govt to be announced next week-Kremlin.
newsitem.headline: New Russian govt to be announced next week-Kremlin.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin is likely to announce a planned government shake-up next Monday or Tuesday and not before, a Kremlin spokesman said on Friday.

Some Russian media had earlier reported that Yeltsin planned to sign a decree restructuring the cabinet on Friday. But the spokesman told Reuters: "There will be nothing today." Most probably the changes would be announced after Yeltsin met Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Monday or Tuesday, he added.

Kremlin press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky was quoted by Itar-Tass news agency as saying Yeltsin would meet Chernomyrdin on Monday or Tuesday before flying to Helsinki on Wednesday for a summit with U.S. President Bill Clinton.
"Probably after this meeting (with Chernomyrdin) the presidential decree on reorganising the cabinet will be made public," Tass said.

Yeltsin, making a comeback after eight months of illness, demanded sweeping government changes last week to address a deepening social and economic crisis. He named his liberal chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais as first deputy to Chernomyrdin.

Yeltsin said on Friday the new government would be "cardinally different" from the previous one, though some of its members would keep their posts. "The most important thing is that the people who will come will have new, fresh ideas and thoughts," Interfax news agency quoted him as saying.
He added that among the new cabinet members would be "people from the regions, those who have done well recently".
Itar-Tass news agency quoted Yeltsin as saying the new government would include seven deputy prime ministers.
The old government structure had three first deputies to Chernomyrdin and nine deputies. The Kremlin says Chubais will be the one and only first deputy prime minister.

The number of deputy premiers mentioned by Yeltsin on Friday appeared higher than indicated in previous leaks from the Kremlin, which made clear Chubais wanted a united team of allies at the top of the cabinet.
This could mean that Yeltsin has decided to keep some of the older guard in the government.
